title: Analog Circuits (OP-AMP)

notes.heading: 1. Ideal OP-AMP Specifications, CMRR & Slew Rate
notes.proseLatex: An ideal operational amplifier has open-loop differential gain $A_{\text{OL}} = \infty$, input impedance $R_{\text{in}} = \infty$ (so input terminal currents are $i_+ = i_- = 0$), output impedance $R_{\text{out}} = 0$, bandwidth $\text{BW} = \infty$, $\text{CMRR} = \infty$, and slew rate $\text{SR} = \infty$ (practical IC 741: $A_{\text{OL}}\sim 10^5,\; R_{\text{in}}\sim 2\text{ M}\Omega,\; R_{\text{out}}\sim 75\,\Omega,\; \text{SR}\approx 0.5\text{ V}/\mu\text{s}$). Common-Mode Rejection Ratio is $\text{CMRR} = \left|\frac{A_d}{A_{\text{cm}}}\right|$ ($20\log_{10}|A_d/A_{\text{cm}}|\text{ dB}$). Slew rate $\text{SR} = \left|\frac{dv_o}{dt}\right|_{\max}$ limits undistorted sinusoidal peak $V_m$ at frequency $f$ via $2\pi f V_m \le \text{SR}$.

keyFormulas.label: CMRR (dB) & Slew-Rate Undistorted Frequency Limit
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Calculate CMRR in dB and maximum undistorted sine-wave frequency/amplitude.

examples.problemLatex: An op-amp has differential gain $A_d = 10^5$ and common-mode gain $A_{\text{cm}} = 0.1$. Find its $\text{CMRR}$ in $\text{dB}$.

notes.heading: 2. Virtual Short & Inverting, Non-Inverting, Buffer & Summing Gains
notes.proseLatex: ONLY under NEGATIVE feedback (output fed back to the $-$ input without rail saturation!), high $A_{\text{OL}}$ forces the virtual-short condition $v_- = v_+$ together with $i_- = i_+ = 0$. Grounding $v_+ = 0$ creates a virtual ground at $v_- = 0$, giving: Inverting amplifier $v_o = -\frac{R_f}{R_1}v_{\text{in}}$ (input resistance $= R_1$); Summing amplifier $v_o = -R_f\sum\frac{v_k}{R_k}$; Non-inverting amplifier $v_o = \left(1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}\right)v_{\text{in}}$; and Voltage Follower / Buffer ($R_f = 0, R_1 = \infty \implies A_v = +1$, high $Z_{\text{in}}$ to low $Z_{\text{out}}$ impedance matching!).

keyFormulas.label: Inverting, Non-Inverting, Summing & Subtractor Equations
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Solve any op-amp resistor network in 15 seconds via v- = v+ and KCL at node v-.

examples.problemLatex: In a non-inverting op-amp circuit powered by $\pm 15\text{ V}$ rails, $R_1 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_f = 8\text{ k}\Omega$, and $v_{\text{in}} = +2\text{ V}$. Find $v_o$.
stepsLatex: $v_o = 5 \times 2\text{ V} = +10\text{ V}$ (within $\pm 15\text{ V}$ rails, so linear!).

notes.heading: 3. Integrator, Differentiator, Comparator & Schmitt Trigger
notes.proseLatex: Replacing feedback $R_f$ with capacitor $C$ creates an inverting INTEGRATOR $v_o(t) = -\frac{1}{RC}\int v_{\text{in}}\,dt$ (converts a square wave into a TRIANGULAR wave, acting as a low-pass filter); swapping $R$ and $C$ creates a DIFFERENTIATOR $v_o(t) = -RC\frac{dv_{\text{in}}}{dt}$ (high-pass, amplifies high-frequency noise). Open-loop or POSITIVE feedback drives output to $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$: an open-loop comparator switches at one threshold, whereas a positive-feedback Schmitt trigger introduces HYSTERESIS ($V_{\text{UTP}} \neq V_{\text{LTP}}$) for noise immunity and converts sine waves into clean square waves!

keyFormulas.label: Op-Amp Integrator, Differentiator & Gain-Bandwidth Product
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Predict square/triangular waveform conversions and closed-loop bandwidth.

In a non-inverting op-amp circuit powered by $\pm 15\text{ V}$ rails, $R_1 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_f = 8\text{ k}\Omega$, and $v_{\text{in}} = +2\text{ V}$. Find $v_o$.

wbjeebTraps: POSITIVE feedback vs NEGATIVE feedback trap: ALWAYS check whether $R_f$ connects to the $-$ terminal (linear virtual short!) or the $+$ terminal (Schmitt trigger saturating at $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$ — virtual short FAILS!).
Supply rail clipping: even in a linear amplifier with gain $+10$, if $v_{\text{in}} = 2\text{ V}$ and rails are $\pm 12\text{ V}$, output clips at $+12\text{ V}$ (NOT $+20\text{ V}$)!
Remember the $+1$ in non-inverting gain $1 + R_f/R_1$ (can NEVER have magnitude $< 1$, unlike inverting $-R_f/R_1$).
